testpilot-final-primary-open_prs.title: fix(model): retain retry and report handling for response timeouts
testpilot-final-primary-open_prs.body:
## Problem

A model response that sends headers and then stalls can raise native `TimeoutError` directly. TestPilot previously skipped its configured retry policy and leaked that exception before the CLI wrote a result or reports. Independent receiving also exposed a second existing boundary: a timeout while reading a terminal HTTP error's diagnostic body escaped from inside the HTTPError handler.

## Change

Update only `OpenAICompatClient.chat` to handle direct transport timeouts through the existing shared retry counter and backoff. Exhaustion becomes a chained `ModelError`, which the existing loop receives normally.

When a terminal HTTP error's diagnostic body stalls, retain the known HTTP status and HTTPError cause, close that response and report `response body timed out`. The already-decided retry budget stays intact: HTTP 400 remains one request, and an exhausted 503 does not start another retry cycle.

Add ten regression cases in `tests/test_model_timeouts.py` and compact source/native qualification under [the receiving directory](docs/receipts/model-timeouts-3dcb83a1-20261008/README.md). Ownership is recorded in [issue 2](https://github.com/Jacob-Met/testpilot/issues/2#issuecomment-6056997400).

## Qualification

The final source is composed with integrated main `f350150259c00dd25c43a95d65157022612d15a8`, including its current CLI, match selector, loop and sandbox.

- Original source: the initial eight new cases produce six failures and two inherited-behavior passes.
- First candidate: 15/15 initial new and existing model cases pass. The two subsequently added terminal-body cases still fail with bare TimeoutError.
- Final candidate: **17/17** (ten new plus seven existing model cases), zero errors or skips.
- Independent, unchanged four-method native receiver: original and first candidate each have one pass and three failures; final candidate **4/4**, zero errors or skips. Its real urllib fixture sends a partial error body before stalling.
- The independent current CLI control returns exit 1 with `model_error`, writes `report.json`, `report.md` and `testpilot.patch`, preserves authored input source and leaks no exception. This control fails at the planner; it does not claim pytest execution.
- The author's separate original CLI controls exercise real native pytest: recovery produces three passing tests and an applicable patch; later repair exhaustion retains the generated failing-test patch and both reports.

Tests use authored localhost responses and record requested backoff. No provider calls are involved. No full-suite, hosted-CI, installation or deployment result is inferred.

## Exact receiving identity

Final head: `bcebf2445f6c32f3120dd81e4bdbd1b90bc05e30`  
Tree: `3b4b217566b75dcbf836cf7b553f50f6aad4cd88`

| File | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `testpilot/model.py` | `f6ae697f1f5d686ffdcb96f5451d1a9600d7d41c7bcf324d7e8c276a107e8673` |
| `tests/test_model_timeouts.py` | `9a5160e63970c39081770e0d35ea0a7dc85a45fb2fd03bdd66aef8e1aef95f9c` |
| Independent executable | `59ea8a59bbfe3e3fde97863589df243326fda6960d0eee909d3fa2c352f01ae2` |
| Independent compact results | `b8d9f4856a40b9830dd89e77558f2c89ddd03abba7daba1d1eec3b910550face` |

The seven declared final files match their native pins. All 202 unowned base leaves are preserved. Original and first-candidate source remain in Git, and the compact receipts retain both negative controls and final results.

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_model.py tests/test_model_timeouts.py
```

testpilot-final-primary-claim.title: Execute generated tests alongside the project's configured pytest suite
testpilot-final-primary-claim.body:
Active contribution: estate-86776bb3cdb8 (HAMON coordination #239).

On exact main `9f01fcb6de085850eca00db746380795eb548d62` / tree `34191a66ec22f8630aea83559cfb16f1e464ab3e`, the actual TestPilot CLI reports success with `status=passed` and `tests_written=0` for a project configured with pytest `testpaths=['checks']`. The emitted `tests/test_generated.py` is omitted from that normal discovery. Applying that exact patch and explicitly executing its generated module fails. A developer can therefore receive a purportedly passing patch that was never exercised.

The isolated native correction will ensure the generated tests are collected alongside the existing project suite, retain source-bound collection provenance, and expose an explicit unqualified outcome when no generated cases execute. The same public CLI / actual pytest / emitted-patch controls will distinguish the beforeimage and candidate.

Owned scope: `testpilot/sandbox.py` generated collection and result qualification; new `testpilot/_pytest_generated.py`; the generated-case count and no-tests outcome spans in `testpilot/loop.py`; new `tests/test_generated_collection.py`; narrow README usage; and unique `docs/receiving/generated-collection-86776bb3cdb8/` evidence. PR #1's CI/evaluation timeout and PR #10's provider response retry remain with their owners. Existing diff, path and partial-repair changes are already integrated and will be preserved.

Current ownership was checked against this repository's open PRs and HAMON #140/#143 plus memory #8. Product implementation and independent receiving use separate worker-owned paths. This is a source contribution claim, not production deployment or a native execution lease.

Receive the original author's unchanged workflow and eval timeout contribution. The current Python inputs pass all 136 tests; the incoming offline replay demo is preserved in full. Expected composed tree 2609ac32021e4cb994fa603c3e6cf89e4abd7f45. Original-head hosted CI passed; current-main push workflow follows this integration.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,20 @@
+# CI: run the pytest suite (36 unit/integration tests, incl. the scripted eval)
+# on every push to main and every pull request. Actions are SHA-pinned to the
+# live upstream tag tips.
+name: ci
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+  pull_request:
+
+jobs:
+  tests:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - run: pip install "pytest>=8" "coverage>=7"
+      - run: python -m pytest -q

@@ -6,7 +6,12 @@ def test_cases_present():
 
 
 def test_scripted_eval_outcomes():
-    rows = [evaluate_case(c, coverage=False, timeout=5) for c in load_cases()]
+    # timeout=10 matches the eval harness CLI default. The sandbox enforces a
+    # hard wall clock, so a smaller timeout flakes on loaded machines: a
+    # timed-out run consumes script replies (ScriptExhausted -> model_error) or
+    # breaks the bug_revealing re-runs, contradicting the "fixed by
+    # construction" determinism this test asserts.
+    rows = [evaluate_case(c, coverage=False, timeout=10) for c in load_cases()]
     by = {r["case"]: r for r in rows}
     assert by["calc_clamp"]["solved"] and by["calc_clamp"]["rounds_used"] == 1
     assert by["textutil_slugify"]["solved"] and by["textutil_slugify"]["rounds_used"] == 2
